title: feat(R9-UX-7): model status and diagnostics
body:
<!-- ccr-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"tvofi"} -->
R9-UX-7 (lane UX, model status and diagnostics), part of #201. Recovered onto
current `main` from the orphaned handoff `handoff/r9-ux-7` (`226e6fc24`): the
work existed and no pull request was ever opened. Issue #1795 is the lane's
feature issue and was closed by #2010 while this lane was still in flight, so
this body closes nothing; see `## Friction`.

Four changes, per `DESIGN-UX.md` section UX-7:

1. **Learning Model Status** (`sensor.py`, the model-status sensor). Reads the
   learning view the coordinator already publishes. The state is an enum:
   `learning`, `learned` (the heat-loss learner has evidence) or `attention`
   (the COP health alarm). One compact recorded row per learner; the bulky
   per-hour gains, the capacity envelope and the system identification state
   are unrecorded attributes. It adds no coordinator line.
2. **Indoor Temperature (Predicted)** (`sensor.py`). A recorded measurement of
   the plan's next-interval room prediction. A module-level
   `coordinator.predicted_next_room_temp(coord)` calls the existing
   `_predicted_next_room_temp`, so the sensor reports exactly the figure the
   accuracy tracker files. It is unavailable while no plan governs the room,
   and `waiting_for` says why: `first_plan` or `plan_not_in_control`.
3. **Diagnostics** (`diagnostics.py`). The download also carries the last
   diagnosis, the input watchdog's published keys, a plan summary (counts and
   totals, no per-step series) and the published learning view. Every
   `person.*` and `calendar.*` entity id is redacted at any depth, inside a
   message string and inside the opt-in debug bundle.
4. **Card, Health tab: "What the model has learned"**. One row per learner with
   its value, its evidence in words and an evidence bar; a COP alarm in the
   warn tone; a 24-bar internal-gains strip naming its peak hour. The Health
   page's two screenshots are regenerated from the browser test (U5) and the
   alt text names the new rows; see `## Figures` and `## Friction`.

New entities move the README count and the `tests/entities.py` rosters in the
same diff.

## Head

`ab2307794d938f348b2bb3835e0b8e64dd77198c` merges live `origin/main`
`8b495603a` (which is #2119's own merge commit, this PR's just-merged sibling
lane) into the previous head `959e05e762`. Two content conflicts, both
resolved and both read hunk-against-hunk, not merged blind:

- `custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/coordinator.py`: one region, where
  main's side adds four lines — the current re-anchor comment on
  `house_heat_loss_scale` (`#110, _reanchor_house_heat_loss_scale`) — and this
  branch's side is empty (the branch's four-line payment deleted an older,
  stale warning about the same re-anchor). **Main's side taken whole**, the
  rule for a landed sibling; the branch's stale-comment payment is spent.
- `tests/golden/claimed_drift.txt`: the five `coord_*` claims exist on both
  sides with different reasons — main's say UX-6, this branch's say UX-7. The
  claim rule keeps the claims that describe THIS branch's diff: the resolved
  file states the UX-7 reasons (`sensors.indoor_temp_predicted and
  sensors.model_status are published; keys added, no value moved`). Main's
  UX-6 reasons describe main's own diff, and main's committed `coord_*.json`
  fixtures already carry the UX-6 keys, so nothing of main's drift is
  unclaimed by the resolution — `env_drift --all` against `8b495603a` prints
  `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56` / `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56` (`## Figures`).

One record re-record rode the same merge commit: `tests/structure_budgets.json`
`max_class_loc` 8711 -> 8715, `recorded_at` 8b495603a. The branch's four-line
budget payment was exactly the stale-comment deletion whose hunk main's newer
four-line comment replaced, so the coordinator span returns to main's own
measurement; **every budget value in the merged file equals main's** and the
branch's whole budget delta over main is the `recorded_at` line. Nothing is
raised over main and no `*_budgets.json` cell exceeds its value on main.

**The silent-revert sweep** (the sibling-merge trap this merge was resolved
against): over the 13 files both sides touched since `595c23b5` (the branch's
previous main), every line `git diff 595c23b5..8b495603a` adds was checked for
verbatim survival in the merged tree — **0 lost**, except the five UX-6 claim
reason lines above (deliberate, replaced by this branch's own claim of the
same scenarios) and the budget cell above (deliberate, re-recorded to main's
own value). **None of #2119's landed lines are absent from the merge result.**
The three production files this fix's mutation proof reads are byte-unchanged
by the merge in the regions it mutates: `git diff 959e05e762 HEAD --
custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/diagnostics.py` is empty, and sensor.py's
merge delta is confined to #2119's `MonthlySavingsSensor` (lines 492-530),
far from the UX-7 sensor classes.

Earlier heads, for the record: `959e05e762` merges main `595c23b` with no
resolution; `78ed5678` merges `664a4c0`; `01d8542b` merges `d5f5841`;
`4e1c290e` merges the authored code head `27ad9640e` plus the PR's own
delivery row; `27ad9640e` is the repair head — the reviewed head `b5c9e5bbae`
(verdict `root-cause-unanswered`), the golden-fixture and claim repair
(`64ba13e36`) and the mutation-ledger pins (`27ad9640e`); the authored code
head remains `574345d95`.

## Already on main under another shape

None of it was. Measured with
`git grep -l <symbol> origin/main -- custom_components tests docs README.md`
against live `origin/main` `8b495603a`: the model-status sensor, the
predicted-temperature sensor, `_without_private_ids`, `_published_sections`,
`PRIVATE_ENTITY_ID`, and the entity keys `learning_model_status` and
`indoor_temperature_predicted` each answer **0 files**, bare or word-bounded.
The module-level `predicted_next_room_temp` answers **0 files word-bounded**
(`git grep -lE '(^|[^_[:alnum:]])predicted_next_room_temp' origin/main --
custom_components tests docs README.md`) — every bare hit is the private
method `_predicted_next_room_temp`, whose name the bare substring also
matches; the module-level function exists nowhere on `main`. `last_diagnosis`
is absent from main's `diagnostics.py`, and the card's "What the model has
learned" block is absent. `dev/programme/delivery/` carries no row claiming
#1795 as delivered.

## The diagnostics collisions, read against mine

`diagnostics.py` is the one file where main moved into this diff's lines twice
(read against the earlier base; the file is byte-unchanged by the new merge):

- **#2065** added `_VIEWS` and `_never_breaks` and the `draw_range` and
  `probe_install` imports. Untouched by this diff; both sides kept.
- **#2071** replaced `"config": dict(entry.data)` with
  `**config_view(entry.data, entry.options)`, adding `config_view()` and the
  `config_setup` / `config_overridden_by_options` keys.
- **#1940** wrapped the debug bundle in
  `debugger.capped(..., f"{DOMAIN}_{entry.entry_id}_debug")`.

This diff re-indents that same dict literal (to wrap it in
`_without_private_ids`) and adds `**_published_sections(coord)`. The
resolution keeps both.

**The interaction is load-bearing.** #2071 made the export carry
`entry.options` *values*, and the away and holiday options hold the `person.*`
and `calendar.*` ids this diff redacts. So the wrapper covers a surface that
did not exist when it was written:
`_without_private_ids(_coarsen({... **config_view(...) ...}))`, the wrapper
outermost.

## Mutation proof

Carried, on byte-identity: the three production lines it deletes —
`diagnostics.py` `_without_private_ids`'s `str` arm,
`sensor.py` `ModelStatusSensor`'s COP-alarm guard, and
`coordinator.py` `predicted_next_room_temp`'s
`return predict() if callable(predict) else None` (now at `:1013`; the line's
text and its function are byte-unchanged by the merge, and the ledger pins are
anchor-keyed by symbol + digest, so the shift moves no row) — are the same
bytes the proof drove at `e12202d9b`, where the baseline printed `ALL 2267
ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` and each mutant failed exactly its named checks (2, 1
and 3 respectively). `tests/entities.py` at the new head passes `ALL 2303
ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (`## Figures`), so the checks the mutants fail are
present and green on the unmutated tree. The eleven `killed_by` rows are
committed in `27ad9640e` and survive the merge (`## Unpinned sites`); whether
CI's drive re-confirms them at the new head is CI's to report — the local
drive cannot complete on this host (`## Red checks`).

## Null control

`main`'s `custom_components/` with this head's `tests/` — the shape that shows
which checks the implementation, and not another change, satisfies — printed
`21 of 2267 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED` when taken at `d3dbf2c3fc42`, the base the
reviewed head measured against. It is **not re-run at `8b495603a`**: the base
has since moved by #2119, #2173, #2176-78 and #2179, none of which adds a
UX-7 check, and the fifteen UX-7 checks plus the roster checks the two new
entities move are all in the failed set at the named base, which is what the
control exists to show. Absence assertions that pass at the base by
construction are the controls for the presence ones: with no model-status
sensor there is nothing to be unavailable, and with no tank or profile there
is no tank-cooling row.

## Figures

Each line is the command that printed it, run at `ab2307794` against live
`origin/main` `8b495603a` (the merge base; `8b495603a` is an ancestor of the
head, so every three-dot comparison is against main's tip). CI's check-runs at
the pushed head are the authority for anything this host cannot produce.

- `python3 tests/structure.py` -- `STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED`, every cell `ok`.
  The branch's whole `tests/structure_budgets.json` delta over main is the
  `recorded_at` line: `max_class_loc` 8715 <= 8715 with main's own value, and
  nothing raised over main.
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff 8b495603a --workdir "$D"` --
  `MODE: SCOPED -- 22 script(s) run, 11 scoped out`, keyed on the mode line,
  over the 39 changed files.
- `node tests/card_drift.mjs origin/main` -- `origin/main = 8b495603a, tree =
  ab2307794, 40 states`; `39 state(s) moved and claimed, 1 identical`. The
  identical one is `editor_schema`, which renders no stylesheet.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 dev/audit/rounds/round4/D6/claims.py` --
  `claims_extracted=125 claims_checked=125 claims_true=123 claims_false=0
  claims_stale=0 claims_unverifiable=2`; `arch_modules_on_disk=76
  arch_map_listed=76 arch_map_missing=0` (main's merges added a module and
  listed it; the map and the disk agree). `git status --porcelain` empty
  after, so the committed `claims.json`/`claims.md` are this tree's own bytes.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/entities.py` -- `ALL 2303 ENTITY
  CHECKS PASSED` at this head (2267 at the reviewed head's base; the step is
  main's own additions).
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/env_drift.py --all 8b495603a` --
  `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56 scenario(s) checked against 8b495603a136...`;
  `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56 committed fixture(s) still match what this tree
  computes`. This is the check that reads the claimed_drift resolution
  directly, and it is green against the new base.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/deployment_shape.py` -- `ALL
  DEPLOYMENT SHAPE CHECKS PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/debug_collect.py` -- `ALL 70 DEBUG
  COLLECT CHECKS PASSED` (the check that pins `_without_private_ids`'s
  fall-through return).
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/arch_score.py --smoke` -- `ALL 257
  ARCHITECTURE SCORE CHECKS PASSED`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/arch_score_head.py` -- `ALL 15
  ARCHITECTURE SCORE HEAD CHECKS PASSED`.
- `python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff origin/main` -- `dS -0.0017
  WORSENS (inadmissible: coord_footprint 2579->2582)`; see `## Architecture
  score`.
- `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main`
  -- `CI PREDICT: no closures or fast red predicted against 8b495603a136 (a
  data-file read is not seen)`; no `ADDED UNPINNED` line at this head.
- `HPO_PAGES_OUT=docs/img/card HPO_BROWSER_SCOPE=auto node
  tests/card_browser.mjs` (U5, after `python3 tests/plan_view.py`) -- the
  Health pages render **byte-identical to the committed screenshots**:
  `health-light.png` 113974 bytes, `health-dark.png` 113574 bytes, `git
  status` clean over `docs/img/card` after the run's own moves are reverted.
  U5 itself prints `ok`; the run's one failure is the P9 grid (below). The
  same run at this head moves only `advisor-*.png` and `plan-why-*.png`,
  which are stale on `main` already and are not this PR's; they were
  restored, not committed.
- Green locally at this head, each on its own run: `tests/block_duty.py`,
  `tests/config_flow_steps.py`, `tests/doc_claims.py`,
  `tests/finite_boundary.py`, `tests/harness_headers.py` (`ALL 109 HARNESS
  HEADER CHECKS PASSED`), `tests/manual_plan.py`, `tests/plan_view.py`,
  `tests/solar_alignment.py`, `tests/wood_advisor.py`, `tests/md_tables.mjs`,
  `tests/card.mjs` (`ALL CARD CHECKS PASSED`),
  `PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub python3 tests/typing_ruler.py` (`ALL 11
  typing-ruler source checks PASSED`; the mypy census itself is CI's
  `typing` job, `HPO_TYPING_PYTHON` unset here).
- Left to CI (heavy, per tvofi's 2026-10-07 rule): `tests/golden.py`,
  `tests/boost_drift_replay.py`, the required mutation drive and the card
  lanes' full matrix. `tests/features.py` is the known macOS BLAS defect;
  its line is under `## Red checks`.

## Unpinned sites

The eleven sites `python3 tools/pr/ci_predict.py --base origin/main` does not
warn about at this head, pinned in `27ad9640e`, surviving the merge: the pins
are anchor-keyed by symbol + digest, and none of the eleven anchors changed —
`predicted_next_room_temp` and `_without_private_ids` kept their names and
line texts, and the sensor classes are untouched. Ten are killed by
`tests/entities.py` and the `_without_private_ids` fall-through return by
`tests/debug_collect.py` (green above). Site lines at this head, where the
merge shifted them: `coordinator.py:1013` (was 931) for
`predicted_next_room_temp`'s return; `diagnostics.py` 99/101/103/105
unchanged; `sensor.py` 2037/2038/2045 for the predicted sensor's
`_waiting_for` guard, its return and `native_value`'s return, and
2090/2093/2095 for the model-status sensor's no-data guard, COP-alarm guard
and learned/learning return. Each ledger row names its anchor, driver and
before/after; `MUTATION TABLE REFUSED`'s cause (the unclaimed coord drift)
is gone at this base — `env_drift` is green above — so the autofix lane's
baseline is no longer red and CI's drive, not this host's, is the authority
on the verdicts (`## Red checks`).

## Architecture score

`python3 tools/audit/archscore/score.py --diff origin/main` reads
`dS -0.0017 WORSENS (inadmissible: coord_footprint 2579->2582)`.

- coord_footprint 2579 -> 2582: the metric charges every function handed the
  coordinator, one per non-plumbing statement, and this diff adds two such
  functions: `coordinator.predicted_next_room_temp` costs 1 statement and
  `diagnostics._published_sections` costs 2. Each exists so a rule has one
  owner rather than a second copy — the module function is what keeps
  `sensor.py` from re-deriving the prediction the accuracy tracker scores, and
  `_published_sections` is what keeps the diagnostics payload section out of
  the export function. Both read the coordinator through `getattr(coord, ...)`,
  the idiom `coordinator.py` already uses for its module-level helpers
  (`getattr(coord, "_ctx", coord)`, `getattr(coord, "_snapshot_ring", None)`).
  The alternative considered and rejected is a bare
  `return coord._predicted_next_room_temp()` — which the metric excludes
  as plumbing but which drops the tolerance for a coordinator-like object
  without the private method that the rest of that helper set keeps. No
  payment removes the statements without duplicating the prediction rule in
  `sensor.py`, which the design rejects.

## Red checks

The pushed head has no check-runs yet (the head exists locally until the App
push); what follows is the range's redness carried forward and re-answered at
the new head.

- `fast (3.14)`: the red this lane's heads last returned was the unclaimed
  coord drift, answered in `64ba13e36` and now green against the NEW base —
  `env_drift --all 8b495603a` prints `NO UNCLAIMED DRIFT: 56` /
  `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56` (`## Figures`). Two further `fast` defects on this
  range are main-data defects fixed by #2173 and #2179, not this diff.
- `mutation`: the refusal's cause was the eleven undispositioned sites; they
  are pinned in `27ad9640e`, the anchors survive the merge, and `ci_predict`
  prints no unpinned warning at this head. CI's drive reports the verdicts;
  this host's cannot complete (`## Friction`).
- `mutation-autofix`: red at the reviewed head as `skip-measure-failed` — its
  pin drive's baseline `tests/env_drift.py` was itself red on the unclaimed
  coord drift, and a driver red at baseline gives no mutant a verdict, so no
  bot commit came (`ci-autofix.md`: a red autofix means no bot commit; the
  lane never automates survivor triage). Answered at this head by removing
  its blocker: the same baseline is green against the new base (`NO UNCLAIMED
  DRIFT: 56` / `NO STALE FIXTURE: 56`, `## Figures`), and the eleven pins the
  drive was for are committed in the branch (`27ad9640e`, anchor-keyed,
  surviving the merge). Cheaper detector and standing cost:
  `tools/pr/ci_predict.py` (static, seconds) for the unpinned-site class,
  and the baseline's own greenness — `env_drift --all` — for the
  measure-failed class.
- `delivery-status`: red because `dev/programme/delivery/2010.md` reads
  `**open**` for #2010, which merged at 2026-10-10T06:37:58Z. The stale row
  is reported in `## Friction` and not fixed here: the delivery row is the
  orchestrator's to write, and this diff's own row (`dev/programme/delivery/
  2120.md`) is carried unchanged. Cheaper detector: the check itself; the
  fix is a one-cell record edit the merge seat makes at the next wave.
- `pr-contract`: answered by this section, which names every check red on the
  range's heads, and by the body re-take at the new head.
- `tests/card_browser.mjs`: `FAIL P9 grid: no two text runs share ink` --
  **pre-existing at `main`, re-confirmed at this head**: the same command at a
  clean `origin/main` worktree reports the identical failure, and this diff
  adds no chart, axis or tick rule. It went unseen because the grid is scoped
  (`P9 grid MODE: SCOPED` here — 3 card-surface files); `main` has not paid
  this check since the rule landed. Cheaper detector: the same scoped grid,
  which is the check.
- `tests/features.py` (`closures`' recording arm, and `prepr` step 6): the
  known macOS BLAS defect (`R9-RC-BLAS-KERNEL-RED`), not this diff — the
  check compares solver floats and this diff touches no optimizer module. No
  check was weakened and no flag was added. The closures step is pushed
  delegated to CI (`PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1`), disclosed in `## Friction`; the
  diff adds no file any closure reads (`ci_predict`: a data-file read is not
  seen).

## Forward-carry

none: no finding here changes how a later stage must work. The carry in
`dev/programme/carries/carry-1795.json` (third entry, from R9-UX-3) is honoured:
the new Health block reads only an always-available, enabled-by-default sensor,
and nothing is added to `HEALTH_WAITING`.

## Friction

- `gate-scoping.md`: cost: `tests/entities.py` takes the gate lease for its
  own lock self-tests, so it queues behind whichever seat holds it. The
  scoped `closure.py select` at this head read `MODE: SCOPED -- 22 script(s)
  run, 11 scoped out`.
- `gate-scoping.md`: cost: `tools/pr/prepr.sh` step 6b refuses on this host —
  `REFUSE closures -- failed while being recorded: tests/features.py (exit
  1)` — the R9-RC-BLAS-KERNEL-RED platform defect again; no interpreter on
  this M1 runs features green. The push carries the closures step delegated
  to CI (`PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1`), disclosed rather than silent; the diff
  adds no file any closure reads.
- `gate-scoping.md`: cost: `tests/features.py` at a clean `origin/main`
  worktree was started at earlier heads and never reached its summary on
  this host; CI's Linux runner is where the BLAS-kernel arm is settled.
- `claim-files.md`: cost: the `claimed_drift.txt` conflict is the file's
  documented by-hand case (keep the claims that describe THIS branch's diff).
  The five UX-6 reason lines main carried describe main's own diff; main's
  fixtures already hold the UX-6 keys, and the merged tree's `env_drift
  --all` against main is green, which is the read-back that the resolution
  claims nothing of main's and drops nothing still live.
- `delivery-status-tracking.md`: stale: `dev/programme/delivery/2010.md` reads
  `**open**` for #2010, which merged at 2026-10-10T06:37:58Z. Reported, not
  fixed, since the delivery row is the orchestrator's to write.
- `delivery-status-tracking.md`: contradiction: the roster's R9-UX-7 brief
  says the lane's feature issue #1795 "stays open for its other groups", but
  #2010 carried the closing keyword for #1795 and closed it. This body
  therefore closes nothing, and the lane's remaining groups (R9-UX-6,
  R9-UX-8..10) now have no open lane issue.
- `local-drive`: cost: this host's default `python3` is 3.11 and the suite
  needs 3.12+ f-string syntax, so every python figure above ran under the
  `venv-ci` 3.14 interpreter; the pinned Playwright package
  (`1.49.0`, `pw-pkg/node_modules`) and its browser cache were reused, not
  reinstalled.
